description:
As a provisioning service, I need to convert a human-entered bandwidth string into a normalized integer number of Mbps, so downstream rate-limiting logic can work with a single unit.

The function parse_bandwidth(value: str) -> int returns the bandwidth in Mbps.
acceptance_criteria: Parsing is case-insensitive and tolerant of internal spaces (e.g. '1 gbps').
A bare number with no unit (e.g. '50') is treated as Mbps and returns 50.
An unknown unit, a negative value, or unparseable text raises ValueError.
flowchart_mermaid:
flowchart TD
    A[Receive value string] --> B[Trim + lowercase + strip spaces]
    B --> C{Ends with known unit?}
    C -->|kbps/mbps/gbps| D[Set conversion factor]
    C -->|no unit| E[Factor = 1 Mbps]
    D --> F{Numeric part parseable?}
    E --> F
    F -->|no| G[Raise ValueError]
    F -->|yes| H{Number < 0?}
    H -->|yes| G
    H -->|no| I[Return int number * factor]
